bib.title: BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models

legacy_report:
SOURCE: BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models. Junnan Li, Dongxu Li, Silvio Savarese, Steven Hoi (Salesforce Research). This file is arXiv:2301.12597v3, dated 15 Jun 2023. The extracted text names no venue, so treat it as a preprint (ICML 2023 is the published venue, but this PDF does not say so).

COVERAGE: I read all 50,034 of 50,034 chars: the body, the Limitation section, every table (1–9), the appendix hyperparameter tables, the Figure 6/7 pages and the references.

AUDIT OF THE NOTE'S NUMBERS
- 32 learned queries, 32×768 output, 257×1024 frozen features: CONFIRMED. One detail to add: 257×1024 is the example "for ViT-L/14". BLIP-2's other encoder, ViT-g/14, has a different shape, and the paper does not give it.
- One linear layer to the LLM: CONFIRMED. The paper says "a fully-connected (FC) layer to linearly project the output query embeddings Z into the same dimension as the text embedding of the LLM". The projected queries are prepended to the LLM's input text embeddings as "soft visual prompts".
- 188M trainable parameters: CONFIRMED with a caveat. "In total, Q-Former contains 188M parameters", and Table 1 lists BLIP-2 at 188M. But Table 2 gives a much smaller "#TrainableParams" for each zero-shot VQA variant: 103M–108M, with 108M for ViT-g FlanT5XXL. The paper does not explain the gap. The "54x fewer" claim uses 188M (10.2B / 188M ≈ 54). So the note should say "Q-Former, 188M parameters (Table 1)" and not tie 188M to the 65.0 model. Two other figures also differ: fine-tuning trains far more parameters, 1.1B–1.2B in Tables 3–5, because the image encoder is unfrozen.
- VQAv2 zero-shot 65.0 vs Flamingo-80B 56.3: CONFIRMED, but the setup must be stated. 65.0 is the BLIP-2 ViT-g + FlanT5-XXL variant on the VQAv2 test-dev split. That variant has 12.1B total parameters. On the val split the same model scores 65.2. Flamingo80B's 56.3 is also test-dev; it has no val number. The "8.7%" is a gap in percentage points (65.0 − 56.3), not a relative gain. The best OPT variant (ViT-g OPT6.7B) scores 52.6 on test-dev, below Flamingo80B.
- No gain from in-context examples, blamed on single image-caption pretraining: CONFIRMED (Section 5, Limitation). One wording fix: the paper says "single image-text pair per sample", and the data is web image-text pairs with synthetic captions. It also notes that Flamingo reports the same observation.

CLAIMS
- claim: BLIP-2 ViT-g FlanT5-XXL beats Flamingo80B on zero-shot VQAv2 test-dev while training far fewer parameters.

  setup: zero-shot; FlanT5 prompt "Question: {} Short answer:"; beam width 5; length penalty -1

  where: Table 2, p6 (~char 23–26k)
- claim: The Q-Former outputs a fixed bottleneck of 32 query vectors, much smaller than the frozen image features.
  number: 32×768 vs 257×1024
  setup: example given for ViT-L/14; 32 queries, each of dimension 768
  quote: "The size of Z (32 × 768) is much smaller than the size of frozen image features (e.g. 257 × 1024 for ViT-L/14)."
  where: Sec 3.1, p3
- claim: The Q-Former is initialised from BERT-base, with randomly initialised cross-attention every other block, and has 188M parameters, counting the queries.
  number: 188M
  setup: Q-Former only
  quote: "In total, Q-Former contains 188M parameters. Note that the queries are considered as model parameters."
  where: Sec 3.1, p3
- claim: Without first-stage representation learning, zero-shot VQA drops substantially, and OPT suffers catastrophic forgetting.
  number: none (Figure 5 curves only)
  setup: ViT-g with OPT6.7B and with FlanT5-XL, over 80k second-stage iterations

  setup: zero-shot VQAv2, Table 2
  quote: "BLIP-2 ViT-L FlanT5XL 103M 3.4B 62.6 62.3 39.4 44.4" / "BLIP-2 ViT-g FlanT5XL 107M 4.1B 63.1 63.0 40.7 44.2"

LIMITS
- No in-context or few-shot gain on VQA. The authors blame single-pair pretraining samples and plan an interleaved dataset (Sec 5).
- Generation can fail through inaccurate LLM knowledge, a wrong reasoning path, or outdated information (Figure 6 examples: wrong person for a quote, ignoring December weather in Canada, iPhone 11 for an iPhone 14).
- Because the models are frozen, BLIP-2 inherits LLM risks: offensive output, social bias, privacy leakage.
- OK-VQA trails Flamingo80B. The OPT variants trail Flamingo80B on VQAv2 test-dev.
- Not shown: the 257×1024 example covers ViT-L only. Pretraining uses 224×224 images. There is no latency or inference-cost comparison. Trainable parameter counts are inconsistent across tables (188M vs 103–108M) and the paper does not explain why.
- Dated: the comparisons are against 2022 models (Flamingo, BEIT-3). Successors such as LLaVA-style MLP projectors are not covered.

BUILDS ON: BLIP (Li et al., 2022) for the objectives, CapFilt and data. ALBEF (Li et al., 2021) for hard-negative mining and ITM reranking. BERT base (Devlin et al., 2019) for Q-Former initialisation. UniLM (Dong et al., 2019) for the causal mask. CLIP (Radford et al., 2021) ViT-L/14. EVA-CLIP (Fang et al., 2022) ViT-g/14. OPT (Zhang et al., 2022). FlanT5 (Chung et al., 2022). Contrasted with Frozen (Tsimpoukelli et al., 2021) and Flamingo (Alayrac et al., 2022), whose Perceiver Resampler the paper likens to the Q-Former without stage 1.

CODE: No code, only prompts. Zero-shot VQA uses "Question: {} Answer:" for OPT and "Question: {} Short answer:" for FlanT5 (Sec 4.1, p6). Captioning uses the prompt "a photo of" (Sec 4.2; Table 7).

FIGURES
- Fig 2, p3: "(Left) Model architecture of Q-Former and BLIP-2's first-stage vision-language representation learning objectives..." It shows the three attention masks (ITC, ITM, ITG) side by side, which is much faster than reading the prose.
- Fig 3, p4: "BLIP-2's second-stage vision-to-language generative pre-training..." It shows the FC projection and soft prompts going into a decoder-only LLM vs an encoder-decoder LLM. It is the best single image for "what the model actually sees".
- Fig 5, p7: "Effect of vision-language representation learning..." The w/ vs w/o curves show OPT collapsing without stage 1.
- Fig 6, p12: incorrect-output examples, useful for the failure modes.

PROBLEMS: The extraction is clean. There are no embedded instructions. Small faults in the source itself:
- The Limitation section points to "see Figure 7" for incorrect outputs, but those are in Figure 6; Figure 7 is the VQA fine-tuning architecture.
- Sec 3.4 prints "β1 = 0.9, β1 = 0.98", where the second should be β2.
- Table 1 headers extract run together, but the values are readable.
